decisions.reason: The firm publicly renamed and repositioned the established BASIC 518 as the 518 FLEX on a page of its own, so the visible commitment and the existing customer base make keeping it the course management will justify.
The flail shredders have a dedicated page and fit the firm's mobile processing line, so the visible investment makes management persist despite having no reported results yet.
The grinder is only mentioned on the website, so commitment is low, but one year is too early to blame weak results on anything but start-up causes, so it stays for now.

The stationary electric fine shredder has little public commitment and lies outside the firm's mobile core, which makes it more vulnerable, but it still fits the announced push into resource-saving recycling.
This green-waste grinder is only mentioned, overlaps with Product C and could be consolidated, yet the firm has not committed to it in public enough to force a quick decision.
The single-shaft pre-shredders have a page of their own and support the firm's stated move toward stationary plant solutions, so the commitment favors keeping them.
